arxiv-2011-13015.title: A Widespread Error in the Use of Benford’s Law to Detect Election and Other Fraud
arxiv-2011-13015.creator: Theodore P. Hill
arxiv-2011-13015.description: Abstract The goal of this note is to show that a widespread claim about Benford’s Law, namely, that the range of every Benford distribution spans at least several orders of magnitude, is false. The proof is constructive and concrete examples are presented. 1 Introduction Errors often occur in mathematics, and sometimes these errors pass peer review and are published.

arxiv-2012-14400.title: Interactions of Linguistic and Domain Overhypotheses in Category Learning
arxiv-2012-14400.creator: Luann C. Jung (luju@mit.edu)
arxiv-2012-14400.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Luann C. Jung (luju@mit.edu). For humans learning to categorize and distinguish parts of the world, the set of assumptions (overhypotheses) they hold about potential category structures is directly related to their learning process. In this work we examine the effects of two overhypotheses for category learning: 1) the bias introduced by the presence of linguistic labels for objects; 2) the conceptual ‘domain’ biases inherent in the learner about which features are most indicative of category structure.

arxiv-2107-01584.title: Decoding the DC and optical conductivities of disordered MoS 2 films: an inverse problem
arxiv-2107-01584.creator: F. R. Duarte, S. Mukim, A. Molina-Sánchez, Tatiana G. Rappoport, M. S. Ferreira
arxiv-2107-01584.description: Abstract To calculate the conductivity of a material having full knowledge of its composition is a reasonably simple task. To do the same in reverse, i.e., to find information about the composition of a device from its conductivity response alone, is very challenging and even more so in the presence of disorder.

arxiv-2108-01187.title: Experimental Demonstration of Broadband Reconfigurable Mechanical Nonreciprocity
arxiv-2108-01187.creator: Amin Mehrvarz, Mohammad Javad Khodaei, Amir Darabi, Ahmad Zareei, Nader Jalili
arxiv-2108-01187.description: Abstract Breaking reciprocity has recently gained significant attention due to its broad range of applications in engineering systems. Here, we introduce the first experimental demonstration of a broadband mechanical beam waveguide, which can be reconfigured to represent wave nonreciprocity. This is achieved by using spatiotemporal stiffness modulation with piezoelectric patches in a closed-loop controller.

arxiv-2310-20279.title: Machine learning refinement of in situ images acquired by low electron dose LC-TEM
arxiv-2310-20279.description: Abstract We study a machine learning (ML) technique for refining images acquired during in situ observation using liquid-cell transmission electron microscopy (LC-TEM). Our model is constructed using a U-Net architecture and a ResNet encoder. For training our ML model, we prepared an original image dataset that contained pairs of images of samples acquired with and without a solution present.

arxiv-2503-09874.description: Abstract . Studying collaborative behavior in Mixed Reality (MR) often requires extensive, challenging data collection. This paper introduces MoCoMR , a novel simulator designed to address this by generating synthetic yet realistic collaborative MR data. MoCoMR captures individual behavioral modalities such as speaking, gaze, and locomotion during a collaborative image-sorting task with 48 participants to identify distinct behavioral patterns.

pmc-10696108.title: Cross-cultural validation of the Chinese cultural value scale in tourism
pmc-10696108.creator: Songshan (Sam) Huang, Jian Xu, Jin Wang
pmc-10696108.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study aims to validate the Chinese Cultural Value Scale in Tourism (CCV-T) across cultures, using a sample of 405 Australian tourists. Through the application of Confirmatory Composite Analysis (CCA) within Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), the study demonstrates that the CCV-T scale exhibits excellent measurement qualities, including indicator reliability, construct reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and nomological validity.

pmc-12590743.title: Women’s knowledge and practices regarding urinary incontinence
pmc-12590743.creator: Dina Adel Mostafa, Hanan I Ahmed, Walaa A Mohamed
pmc-12590743.description: BackgroundUrinary incontinence (UI) is a widespread condition affecting a large population globally. Women are disproportionately affected by UI, with the condition becoming more common with advancing age. UI is characterized as involuntary loss of urine during the bladder storage phase, which can significantly diminish a woman’s quality of life and impose substantial societal costs.

pmc-13111406.description: ObjectiveThis study aims to investigate the role of neurotrophin‐4 (NTF4) in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) and to elucidate the underlying mechanism by which NTF4 regulates high glucose‐induced apoptosis and inflammation in HTR‐8/SVneo cells via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.MethodsTranscriptomic analysis combined with public database screening revealed that NTF4 is significantly upregulated in placental tissues from GDM patients.

pmc-13289969.title: Endoscopic closure of a malignant entero-vaginal fistula using a cardiac septal occluder device
pmc-13289969.creator: Patricia Mester, Can-Martin Sag, Vlad Pavel, Martina Müller, Hans-Jürgen Schlitt, Matthias Hornung, Arne Kandulski
pmc-13289969.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cardiac septal occluder (CSO) devices, originally developed for transcatheter closure of atrial and ventricular septal defects 3 , have only recently been investigated as a treatment option for gastrointestinal fistulas 4 . Here, we report the case of a 44-year-old woman with advanced pseudomyxoma peritonei who had previously undergone multiple abdominal operations, including small- and large-bowel resections with end-to-end ileostomy and descending colostomy. At the current admission, she presented with feculent vaginal discharge. Computed tomography (CT) demonstrated an enterovaginal fistula.

pmc-13442593.description: BackgroundEndoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) allows en bloc, organ-sparing removal of large superficial colorectal lesions; however, conventional ESD (C-ESD) is often time intensive, technically challenging, and associated with clinically relevant adverse events. Traction-assisted ESD (TA-ESD) was developed to enhance submucosal visualization and maintain a stable dissection plane.
